name: HippoRAG (Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models)
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (The Thirty-eighth Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems; OpenReview id=hkujvAPVsg). Preprint arXiv:2405.14831 (cs.CL); v1 23 May 2024, v3 14 Jan 2025.
authors_affiliation: Bernal Jimenez Gutierrez, Yiheng Shu, Yu Gu, Yu Su (The Ohio State University); Michihiro Yasunaga (Stanford University). Lead/corresponding from the OSU NLP Group.
code_url: https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG (MIT license; original HippoRAG code tagged v1.0.0 / legacy branch). OpenReview: https://openreview.net/forum?id=hkujvAPVsg
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/OSU-NLP-Group/HippoRAG (actively maintained, ~3.6k stars; the repo main branch has since evolved to HippoRAG 2 'From RAG to Memory', ICML 2025, arXiv:2502.14802; the original HippoRAG 1 is preserved under the 'legacy' branch / v1.0.0 release).
task_domain: QA: multi-hop / knowledge-integration question answering (retrieval-augmented), framed as long-term memory for LLMs.
problem_setting: Offline-indexed, single-agent, non-interactive open-domain multi-hop QA. A retrieval corpus (passages, including supporting and distractor passages following the IRCoT setup) is indexed once offline into a schemaless knowledge graph; at test time a query is answered by retrieving passages and feeding them to a frozen QA reader LLM. No task-level supervision or retriever fine-tuning is used (all components are off-the-shelf); two hyperparameters (synonymy threshold tau=0.8, PPR damping=0.5) are tuned on 100 MuSiQue training examples. The work emphasizes single-step multi-hop retrieval (vs iterative RAG) and a continually-updatable memory (new knowledge integrated by adding edges to the KG rather than re-summarizing).
what_is_retrieved: Passages/documents (ranked via aggregated PageRank node probabilities). The underlying retrievable store is an open knowledge-graph index of noun-phrase entity nodes and relation edges (OpenIE triples) plus synonymy edges; passages are scored from the KG node probabilities.
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus: an LLM-derived open KG (artificial hippocampal index) built offline over the document corpus. Authors note the KG can be incrementally updated by adding edges (continually-updating memory), but in the reported experiments it is a fixed corpus index, not a self-written episodic agent memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Both a fixed top-k ranking objective (R@2/R@5) AND an explicit completeness objective: the paper introduces an 'all-recall' metric (AR@2/AR@5) measuring the percentage of queries for which ALL supporting passages are retrieved, arguing HippoRAG's advantage is single-step recovery of the complete supporting set (gap over ColBERTv2 grows from ~20% to ~38% R@5 on 2Wiki when measured by all-recall).
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not a case-based reasoning system; no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain case cycle).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work frames itself via the hippocampal memory indexing theory (neuroscience) and KG+PageRank retrieval, not as case-based reasoning; it does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: KG-subgraph -> passage/document. The index is built from KG units (noun-phrase entity nodes and relation edges = OpenIE triples), and Personalized PageRank scores over these nodes are aggregated (via a |N|x|P| node-passage incidence matrix) to rank passages, which are the final retrieved unit.
index_source: Static corpus, offline-induced: an instruction-tuned LLM (default GPT-3.5-turbo-1106) performs OpenIE over each passage to build a schemaless open KG; off-the-shelf retrieval encoders (Contriever or ColBERTv2) add synonymy edges between similar noun phrases. The store is built offline once (though the authors highlight that new passages can be incrementally added by extending the KG with new edges).
index_structure_topology: Knowledge GRAPH: a schemaless open KG with noun-phrase entity nodes, OpenIE relation edges, and additional synonymy edges between near-duplicate phrases (the 'artificial hippocampal index'). A node-to-passage incidence matrix links graph nodes back to source passages.
retriever_type: Hybrid graph-based: LLM-as-extractor (OpenIE for indexing; query NER for retrieval) + dense retrieval encoder (Contriever or ColBERTv2) for entity linking / synonymy edges + Personalized PageRank graph search for the actual ranking. No learned/trained retriever module.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf). All components (LLM for OpenIE/NER, dense encoders, PPR) are used without training or fine-tuning. Only two scalar hyperparameters (synonymy threshold tau=0.8 and PPR damping factor=0.5) are tuned on 100 MuSiQue training examples; node specificity provides an unsupervised IDF-like weighting.
query_construction: Intent/entity extraction: the LLM ('neocortex') extracts a set of salient query named entities from the raw query via 1-shot prompting; these are encoded by the retrieval encoder and linked to their most similar KG nodes (query nodes), which become the PPR seed set. No sub-query decomposition or query rewriting in the single-step setting.
query_granularity: Task-level (one-shot at t=0): a single query-time entity extraction + one PPR run per query. (When wrapped inside IRCoT for the multi-step variant, retrieval becomes trajectory/step-level, but core HippoRAG is single-shot.)
when_to_retrieve: One-shot (single-step retrieval): a single PPR-based retrieval pass per query, performing multi-hop reasoning in one step. The paper's central claim is replacing iterative retrieval (IRCoT) with single-step retrieval; HippoRAG can also be plugged into IRCoT to enable iterative retrieval for further gains.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed schedule: retrieval is always performed once per query (no confidence/uncertainty/learned trigger). In the IRCoT+HippoRAG variant, the trigger is IRCoT's fixed iterative reason-then-retrieve loop (2-4 rounds in their experiments).
reranking: No explicit cross-encoder/reranking stage in HippoRAG 1. Ranking is produced directly by aggregating Personalized PageRank node probabilities over passages (weighted by node specificity, an IDF-like local signal). ColBERTv2, when used, serves as a synonymy-edge encoder, not a downstream reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: None beyond passage ranking: PPR distributes probability from query nodes across the KG and the aggregated node probabilities directly rank passages; node specificity (IDF-like) reweights node contributions. No decompose-recompose, distillation, or compression of retrieved passages.
index_content_separation: Partial / implicit: a lightweight graph index (entity nodes + edges, the hippocampal index) is separated from the heavy passage content, and passages are only surfaced after PPR scoring via the node-passage incidence matrix. Not a formal progressive-disclosure/SOP-index-then-content protocol.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR system; no retrieved-case adaptation/revision). Retrieved passages are used verbatim as context for the QA reader.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation: the top-ranked passages are fed to a separate frozen QA reader LLM (with the same reader/prompt across methods) to generate the answer. Retrieval and generation are decoupled (HippoRAG improves QA only indirectly by improving retrieval).
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-read (no agentic planning in core HippoRAG): a single retrieval step feeds a QA reader. The multi-step variant interleaves HippoRAG retrieval inside IRCoT's iterative chain-of-thought reason-then-retrieve loop.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-answer for single-step HippoRAG (one retrieval, one read). When integrated with IRCoT, retrieval is interleaved per-CoT-reasoning-step (per IRCoT iteration).
retrieved_item_representation: Raw passages/document text injected into the QA reader's prompt. The intermediate representation that drives ranking is structured (KG nodes/edges + PPR probabilities), but what is injected for generation is raw passage text.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw passages (single retrieval unit) ranked via structured graph associations. The retrieval signal is built on a distilled associative structure (open KG triples), but the retrieved/injected unit is the original passage, not a distilled strategy or summary (explicitly contrasted with summarization-based methods like RAPTOR/GraphRAG).
noise_robustness_mechanism: Node specificity (an IDF-like local weighting that down-weights nodes appearing in many passages) and synonymy-edge construction (noisy entity standardization) improve robustness; PPR's restart/damping concentrates probability around query-node neighborhoods, mitigating spurious activations. No retriever-aware training or learned relevance evaluator. Error analysis attributes most errors to NER/OpenIE extraction and to PPR struggling when many passages discuss similar topics.
memory_type: graph (a schemaless open knowledge-graph 'artificial hippocampal index' that serves as long-term memory). Static corpus index in the experiments, designed to be incrementally extendable.
write_back: False (in the reported experiments): the KG index is built offline and the system does not write back query-time answers/experiences into memory. The framework is designed to support adding new knowledge by inserting new OpenIE triples/edges into the KG, but this incremental-update capability is described conceptually rather than evaluated as test-time write-back.
online_growth: Not in the evaluated setting (corpus indexed offline, frozen at test time). The paper argues HippoRAG can continuously integrate new knowledge by adding edges to its KG (vs re-summarizing as in RAPTOR/GraphRAG), positioning it as a continually-updating memory, but online growth is not empirically benchmarked in HippoRAG 1.
write_back_trigger: Never (at query/test time in the experiments). New-knowledge integration is an offline indexing operation (add OpenIE triples/synonymy edges for new passages), not triggered by on-success/on-failure/reflective query-time events.
failure_experience_usage: Not applicable / not used. The system stores no success/failure experiences; there is no experience memory. (A qualitative error analysis of 100 MuSiQue errors is reported but not fed back into the system.)
memory_evolution_update: Append/extend (conceptual): new knowledge is integrated by adding nodes/edges to the KG; synonymy detection performs a form of dedup/standardization between near-duplicate phrases at indexing time. No post-write mutation, refine-overwrite, or forgetting is evaluated.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval is a fixed graph algorithm (Personalized PageRank seeded by similarity-linked query nodes), not a learned or RL-optimized retrieval/selection policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent, single private corpus index; no multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: MuSiQue (answerable), 2WikiMultiHopQA (2Wiki), and HotpotQA. 1,000 questions sampled from each validation set; a retrieval corpus per dataset is formed from all candidate (supporting + distractor) passages following IRCoT (corpus sizes: MuSiQue 11,656 passages; 2Wiki 6,119; HotpotQA 9,221). A small path-finding multi-hop QA case study is also constructed.
benchmark_family: multi-hop QA (open-domain multi-hop question answering / knowledge integration).
baselines: Single-step retrievers: BM25, Contriever, GTR, ColBERTv2, Propositionizer (Proposition), RAPTOR (and RAPTOR/Proposition with ColBERTv2 backbone). Multi-step: IRCoT (with BM25 / Contriever / ColBERTv2). QA readers compared: None (closed-book), ColBERTv2, IRCoT, and IRCoT+HippoRAG, all with the same reader. Ablation/alternative components: REBEL (end-to-end OpenIE), Llama-3.1-8B/70B-Instruct (OpenIE), and PPR alternatives (query-nodes-only; query-nodes+neighbors).
key_metrics: Retrieval: Recall@2 (R@2) and Recall@5 (R@5); plus all-recall AR@2/AR@5 (fraction of queries where ALL supporting passages are retrieved). QA: Exact Match (EM) and F1. Efficiency: online retrieval API cost ($) and latency (minutes), reported as 10-30x cheaper / 6-13x faster than IRCoT.
headline_result: On 2WikiMultiHopQA, single-step HippoRAG improves single-step retrieval by ~11 points R@2 and ~20 points R@5 over the strongest baselines (e.g., HippoRAG-Contriever 71.5 R@2 / 89.5 R@5 vs ColBERTv2 59.2 / 68.2), with ~3% gains on MuSiQue and competitive results on HotpotQA; it matches or beats iterative IRCoT while being 10-30x cheaper and 6-13x faster in online retrieval. The abstract's single-number claim: outperforms state-of-the-art by up to 20%.
ablations: Table 5 dissects HippoRAG (R@2/R@5 over the 3 datasets). OpenIE alternatives: REBEL causes large drops (avg 46.2/58.4 vs HippoRAG 57.4/72.9), showing LLM OpenIE flexibility matters; Llama-3.1-8B is competitive except on 2Wiki, Llama-3.1-70B (avg 57.1/72.5) roughly matches GPT-3.5. PPR alternatives: replacing PPR with query-nodes-only (50.7/56.2) or query-nodes+neighbors (42.2/59.2) is much worse, confirming PPR drives multi-hop association (notably, adding neighbors without PPR hurts vs nodes-only). Component ablations: removing node specificity drops avg to 54.7/70.9 (largest effect on MuSiQue/HotpotQA); removing synonymy edges drops to 56.2/70.5 (largest effect on 2Wiki). All-recall (Table 6) shows the gap over ColBERTv2 grows (e.g., 2Wiki R@5 gap ~20% -> ~38%). Intrinsic OpenIE eval (CaRB) on 239 gold MuSiQue triples corroborates extraction quality.
evaluation_decoupling: Yes. Intrinsic retrieval metrics (R@2/R@5, plus the all-recall AR@2/AR@5 completeness metric and a CaRB-based intrinsic OpenIE evaluation) are reported separately from end-to-end QA metrics (EM/F1); the paper explicitly attributes QA gains to retrieval improvements with a shared reader.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Outcome: QA EM/F1. Process/intermediate: retrieval R@k, the all-recall metric (whether ALL supporting passages, i.e. successful multi-hop reasoning, are recovered), intrinsic OpenIE precision/recall/F1, and a qualitative error analysis (NER vs OpenIE vs PPR error categories).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Online retrieval (1,000 queries, GPT-3.5 Turbo, Table 17): HippoRAG ~$0.1 and ~3 min vs IRCoT ~$1-3 and ~20-40 min (ColBERTv2 ~$0 / ~1 min) => 10-30x cheaper, 6-13x faster than IRCoT. Tradeoff: offline indexing is heavier for HippoRAG (~$15 and ~60 min more per 10,000 passages with GPT-3.5; Llama-3.1-70B via vLLM on 4xH100 indexes 10,000 docs in ~250 min / ~4 hours at $0 API). The persistent advantage is online retrieval token count (only query NER vs reprocessing all retrieved docs).
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed top-k passage budget: retrieval evaluated at k=2 and k=5 (R@2/R@5; QA reader fed the top retrieved passages). No adaptive/precision-driven variable-k; HippoRAG ranks all passages by aggregated PPR probability then truncates to k.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Uses existing datasets (MuSiQue, 2WikiMultiHopQA, HotpotQA), sampling 1,000 questions per validation set and building a per-dataset retrieval corpus from all candidate passages following IRCoT (11,656 / 6,119 / 9,221 passages). Extracted KG statistics reported (e.g., MuSiQue ~91,729 nodes, ~107,448 triples). A small additional path-finding multi-hop QA case study is hand-constructed (book/movie + trait queries with Wikipedia distractors). Answers verified via EM/F1 against gold answers.
builds_on: Retrieval-augmented generation (Lewis et al., 2020); the hippocampal memory indexing theory (Teyler & Discenna, 1986); Personalized PageRank (Haveliwala, 2002 / Page et al.); open information extraction (OpenIE); dense retrievers Contriever (Izacard et al.), ColBERTv2 (Santhanam et al.), GTR (Ni et al.); IRCoT (Trivedi et al., 2023) for the realistic-corpus setup and as the iterative-retrieval method it both compares against and augments; LLM OpenIE via GPT-3.5 / Llama-3.1.
contrasts_with: Iterative/multi-step RAG, especially IRCoT (HippoRAG achieves comparable accuracy in a single step at far lower cost/latency, and can also augment IRCoT). Standard single-step dense retrievers (BM25, Contriever, GTR, ColBERTv2) that encode passages in isolation and cannot integrate knowledge across passage boundaries. LLM-augmented indexing-time summarization methods RAPTOR, GraphRAG, MemWalker (which must re-summarize when new data is added, whereas HippoRAG just adds KG edges). Parametric memory / model editing and long-context-as-memory approaches.
lineage: Group B / RAG for task solving and Group F (decision/memory) boundary: a static-corpus graph-RAG method (KG + Personalized PageRank) positioned as non-parametric long-term memory for LLMs. Pioneers single-step multi-hop graph retrieval as a cheaper alternative to iterative RAG; direct predecessor of HippoRAG 2 ('From RAG to Memory', ICML 2025) and influential in the graph-based RAG / LLM-memory line.
